mappings.note: Places construction in the secondary sector. LO-322 is the frame's only outcome about the kinds of work people do, and the sector classification is exactly a grouping of occupations.
Factory manufacturing such as milling grain classed as secondary - another occupation-grouping item, so LO-322.
Turning farm cotton into cloth in a mill as secondary work; the classification of a named kind of job, hence LO-322.
The tertiary sector as the one supporting primary and secondary work - the relation between families of occupations, so LO-322.
Doctors, teachers and lawyers placed in the tertiary sector; naming occupations and their sector, so LO-322.
Defines a warehouse as a store for goods before sale - market vocabulary, which belongs to CG-SST4's institutions rather than to the occupations outcome.
Anand farmers losing milk to spoilage before AMUL: a market failure (CG-SST4) facing a rural occupation (LO-322).
Defines and contrasts primary and secondary sectors with examples - the fullest statement of the occupation grouping in the chapter, so LO-322.
How secondary work leans on tertiary services; interdependence between families of occupations, hence LO-322.
A flow diagram of the dairy chain across all three sectors - the same interdependence, worked as a single example, so LO-322.
Kautilya's Arthashastra making economic activity the root of prosperity: an idea from an ancient text (LO-311) about the economy (CG-SST4). Not LO-322: no occupation is classified.
How the range of economic activity has widened from early societies to today - the growth in the variety of available occupations (LO-322) within a changing economy (CG-SST4).
Defines 'economic sector' as a grouping of similar activities; the organising idea behind the occupation classification, so LO-322.
Names primary, secondary and tertiary as the three sectors - the classification itself, hence LO-322.

Coal mining as primary extraction; the same sector-placement demand, hence LO-322.
Defines middlemen as intermediaries buying low from producers and selling high - how the market worked against the farmers, so CG-SST4.
Defines a cooperative as a jointly owned, democratically run association - an economic institution, which CG-SST4 covers.
Verghese Kurien alongside Tribhuvandas Patel in founding AMUL: a fact about the cooperative institution, so CG-SST4.
What farmers gained by joining AMUL - control over processing and marketing, and the loss of the middleman: the cooperative changing their place in the market, so CG-SST4.
Defines a factory as the plant where goods are manufactured - an economic institution, so CG-SST4. The sector such work belongs to is asked separately and mapped to LO-322.
Defines export as selling abroad what is produced at home; a market concept, so CG-SST4. Not LO-323, whose contacts are in religion, art and architecture rather than trade.
Milking cows for sale classed as primary - sector placement of a named rural occupation, so LO-322.
AMUL turning milk into powder, ghee and cheese as secondary work. The printed answer has been overrun by an unrelated matching key, but the question is a clean sector-placement item.
A matching set running livestock rearing, milk processing and dairy retail across the three sectors (LO-322) and ending with the cooperative as a producers' institution (CG-SST4).
Defines monetary value as worth measurable in money - the market vocabulary on which the chapter rests, so CG-SST4.
Names one of the three sectors; the classification itself, hence LO-322.
The primary sector as the one directly dependent on nature - a sector-definition item, so LO-322.

Factory manufacturing placed in the secondary sector - the same sector-placement demand, so LO-322.
Turning forest wood into furniture as secondary work; sector placement of a named craft, hence LO-322.
The tertiary sector as support to primary and secondary workers - the interdependence point, so LO-322.
'Service sector' as the other name for tertiary; sector vocabulary, so LO-322.
A truck driver's transport service placed in the tertiary sector - sector placement of a named occupation.
Doctors, nurses, teachers and lawyers in the tertiary sector; the short-answer twin of the earlier professions item.
Names warehouses as the buildings where goods wait to be sold - market vocabulary, so CG-SST4 with the other institution items.
Finds 'doctor - primary' false among livestock, automobiles and trucking: a sector-placement check across four occupations, so LO-322.
Orders cotton farming, mill weaving and retail selling as primary, secondary and tertiary - the clearest sector-sequence item in the chapter, hence LO-322.
